# Narrated read and stage actions: report-runner aftermath retry

No tools are available. Each step below describes a required read or an intended action. No live calls were made. Command and dispatch text is quoted, not executed. Outcomes come only from the fixed observations.

## Main trace (git)

1. **Re-read section 5.** `read` `<skills root>/skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md` (section 5, "Apply, aftermath, commit") before the aftermath. The observations do not report this read's result. The rest of this trace assumes it succeeds. If it were unreadable, this would be a blocking stop with no aftermath from memory.

2. **Classify the outcome.** Per the fixed observations, this batch is on the ordinary `Amend:` aftermath route. Writing-plans already ran its first `Findings:` retry. The second parent `plan_check` FAIL is identical to the first, so it enters the attribution check.
   - The FAIL lines quote `Tests: \`node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit\``.
   - The owning Task 1 has `Spec: doc/specs/report-runner.md#tests`, which is the amended Tests section.
   - The observed `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md` shows Task 1 Tests as `node --test eval/lib/lint.test.mjs`.
   - So this batch changed that text, and the FAIL is attributable.

3. **Check the dirtied row.** The writer also returned a `dirtied tracked source` row. Its baseline command, `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`, is the same text this batch introduced, so the row is also attributable.
   - The row folds into one item. It is the first aftermath item, so it is within the two-item limit.
   - Its evidence does not repeat the evidence of the applied "Run report replay" item.
   - It is not redraw-class: Goal, Problem, ACs and boundaries are unchanged.

4. **Check every dirtied path.** The three membership checks are:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   - Each prints its path, so all three are tracked.
   - None of them is the spec, the plan, or an `In-flight:` path.
   - There is no `??` at a `Create:`/`Test:` path.
   - So the row is eligible for restore.
   - The `artifacts:` path `/tmp/report-runner-artifacts/audit.log` lies outside the row and is preserved, as are the `In-flight:` paths.

5. **Hold the item.**

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Handle | `replay` |
   | Title | Move replay to verification |
   | Location | Tests (the amended section) |
   | Change | old `replays in Task 1 Tests` -> new `replays at final verification` |
   | Recommended | `accept` (no alternatives) |
   | Evidence | the verbatim FAIL lines (below) plus the dirtied row |

   The FAIL lines, verbatim:
   ```
   FAIL (1 findings)
   command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
   > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
   ```

6. **Re-read the grant.** `read` the Standing grants section (section 1's predicate and Value decoding) in the same `amendment-surface.md`. Re-reading the spec header shows `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends`, unchanged.
   - The value is well-formed and decodes to amend permission, so the recommended edit applies without asking.
   - This grant never authorizes a redraw, and it never authorizes restoring a path on its own.

7. **Restore exactly the eligible paths** before applying this retry. One quoted path per command, in the explicit worktree:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   - Each exits 0. A nonzero exit would stop and print the shell error.
   - The orchestrator does this restore, never the plan-writer.

8. **Apply the spec edit.** Change the spec Tests text to `replays at final verification`, then print:
   `amended the spec: Move replay to verification - replays at final verification`

9. **Re-dispatch the plan-writer.** Send an `Amend:`-only re-dispatch:
   > Amend: Tests. Rule: preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks; correct Task 1 because the parent check failed with "command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token / > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`" and the baseline row "`node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json". Replay now runs at final verification.
   > In-flight: doc/specs/report-runner.md, doc/plans/report-runner.md

   Then run the parent steps 5-6 again. The ledger bypass is retained, though no ledger exists. The observed results are PLAN WRITTEN and parent PASS.

10. **Final read.** Read the amended plan once (step 7's read only). There is no phase completion, no `plan_tracker init`, and no edit to the plan text by the main loop.

11. **Update the tracker.** Task 1's anchors changed and it was complete, so call `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1 index>, status: "in_progress" })`.
    - No tasks were added or removed, so there is no re-`init`.
    - There is no `phase_tracker` call; the phase stays implement and no phase completes.
    - Task 1 re-runs the task loop.

12. **Commit once for the batch.** Stage the spec and plan together:
    ```bash
    git -C /tmp/report-worktree add -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md && git -C /tmp/report-worktree commit -q -F - -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md <<'EOF'
    amend: 2 item(s) - Run report replay, Move replay to verification

    - <first handle> | Run report replay | replays in Task 1 Tests | <its recorded choice> | <its reviewer line> | <its evidence>
    - replay | Move replay to verification | replays at final verification | granted | aftermath retry: attributed plan_check FAIL | <verbatim FAIL lines>; <dirtied row>
    "auto-apply amends"
    EOF
    ```

### Audit choice kinds and undo

- **Under the grant**, the aftermath item is recorded as `granted`. `granted` and `auto-apply` records are the ones `finishing-a-development-branch` Step 4's `amend:` digest reads.
- **Without amend permission**, a later human pick would be recorded as `accepted` (for `A`) or `alt-n` (for an alternative). Those records are not digested.
- **To undo**, run `git revert` on this single `amend:` commit. That undoes the retry together with the batch.
  - Then read `**Amend-grant:**` from the pre-revert HEAD with `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD^:doc/specs/report-runner.md`, through the predicate.
  - If the working tree's value differs, restore that value and persist it per Standing grants before re-entering the surface.
  - The source checkouts in step 7 are not part of the commit, so a revert leaves them in place.

## Variant U (independent; same pre-restore state)

- The row also contains `tests/report-new.test.mjs`. It shows as `??`, it is a `Create:`/`Test:` path in the plan, and `ls-files` prints nothing for it. That makes the row ineligible.
- The entire row goes through step 6 with no partial restoration. **None of the original three paths is restored.**
- The step-6 branch is rendered in full:
  - The verbatim FAIL lines are quoted as the open question.
  - It states Task 1 and the command `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`. SHA and exit are not reported in the observed row and are not invented.
  - It offers `fix-first`, `narrow` and `amend` on separate lines, followed by `Recommendation: ...`.
  - It names all four dirty paths and their cause, and hands every path to the human to commit, discard or move.
- It waits for the human. The grant is not consent for restoration.

## Variant P (independent; same pre-restore state)

- The row also contains `doc/specs/report-runner.md`, which is tracked but protected. The same applies if the extra path is the plan or any other `In-flight:` path.
- The whole row goes through step 6 as in U, rendered in full. **None of the original three paths is restored.**

## Variant R (independent; same pre-restore state, same three paths)

- The second FAIL reads `acceptance-scope @ line 24: report runner must also audit refund records...`. Fixing it changes the spec Goal and acceptance criteria, so it is redraw-class.
- Before any restore:
  1. Commit the batch as-is (the "Run report replay" item) as batch preservation.
  2. Hand the three dirty paths to step 6 without restoration.
  3. Take `../SKILL.md`'s redraw path. Narrated read: `read` `<skills root>/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, section "Amending an approved spec". An unreadable file is a blocking stop.
- A redraw still stops for the user even under `auto-apply amends`. I state the redraw call and wait. On confirmation, the redraw keeps the worktree and spec, then:
  - `plan_tracker({ action: "clear" })`
  - `phase_tracker({ action: "reset" })`
  - `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "brainstorm" })`
  - delete the plan file (there is no ledger)
  - resume at checklist step 4

## Plain-jj equivalent of the restore

Use this instead of the git checkout, never both, with one path per command. The `root:` fileset anchors the path at the workspace root, because `-R` alone does not change cwd-relative path resolution:

```bash
jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
```

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### Main git trace

1. **Required reference read.** Narrate a fresh `read` of `skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md`, section 5, using its absolute installed path—not a shell command. The bundled reference is not a session read. No unreadable-reference observation is supplied here; if that required read were unreadable, stop before restoration or application.

2. **Classify and attribute the findings.** The fixed HEAD-plan observation comes from:
   ```sh
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   HEAD used the lint test; the current plan uses the report audit after this batch changed **Tests** to require Task 1 replay. Compare that changed command text and the amended Tests contract—not merely Task 1’s membership or its line number. Hold the newly selected audit command’s findings in this uncommitted batch. Do not solve the replay’s source mutation merely by adding the missing `Test:` token.

   Returning replay to final verification changes Tests inside the existing component. It does not change Goal, Problem, ACs, or boundaries, so it is an **amend**, not a redraw or descope.

3. **Hold the retry item.**
   - Handle: `replay`
   - Title: Move replay to verification
   - Location: Tests
   - Change: `replays in Task 1 Tests` → `replays at final verification`
   - Recommendation: `accept`; no alternatives
   - Evidence, retained verbatim:
     ```text
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json
     ```
   This is the first aftermath item; the original “Run report replay” amendment is not an aftermath retry.

4. **Read and acknowledge the grant.** Required narrated reads cover Standing grants and the spec header through its predicate and Value decoding. The supplied re-read observation remains:
   ```text
   **Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends
   ```
   Acknowledge that exact value. It authorizes the recommended amend, not a redraw or general cleanup.

5. **Establish restoration eligibility before applying the retry.** The three quoted `ls-files` checks each print their exact path:
   ```sh
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   All are tracked and outside the spec, plan, and In-flight set. The external artifact is not part of this row and must remain untouched.

6. **Intended exact restoration, before the retry edit.**
   ```sh
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   The fixed observations say each succeeds with exit 0. A nonzero result would stop with the actual shell error. Restoration stays with the parent, not the writer.

7. **Apply under the grant**, then narrate:
   ```text
   amended the spec: Move replay to verification - move replay from Task 1 Tests to final verification
   ```
   Preserve all unrelated working-tree changes.

8. **Intended corrected dispatch.** Send the plan-writer an **Amend-only** retry, preserving unaffected task titles and wave positions:
   ```text
   Amend:
     Sections: Tests
     Rule: Move replay to final verification; repair only affected anchors
     and tasks. Preserve unaffected task titles and wave positions.
     Evidence:
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json
   In-flight:
     doc/specs/report-runner.md
     doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   The supplied subsequent observations are `PLAN WRITTEN`, then parent `PASS`.

9. **Finalize once, in order.** After PASS, narrate the final `read` of `/tmp/report-worktree/doc/plans/report-runner.md`. Then reopen previously complete Task 1 as `in_progress`, using its resolved tracker index. Do not clear/init the tracker or complete/change a phase. Commit the spec and plan together, once, preserving the whole batch:
   ```text
   amend: 2 item(s) - Run report replay, Move replay to verification
   ```
   The original item retains its actual recorded choice; do not invent one. The retry audit uses `granted`, its evidence, and the quoted granting sentence. A later human-selected correction would instead use `accepted` or `alt-n`, with its evidence. Undo the entire batch with `git revert <batch-commit>`; then perform the required pre-revert-HEAD grant read and reconciliation before re-entering amendments.

### Independent U — untracked new test

10. Reset conceptually to the supplied pre-restore state. The extra `tests/report-new.test.mjs` is `??`, a Create:/Test: path, and its `ls-files` check prints nothing. **Restore none of the row**, including none of the original three paths. Route the entire row to the human to commit, discard, or move the dirt, naming the paths and test-command cause. Do not delegate restoration or retry over unresolved dirt.

### Independent P — protected path

11. The added spec path is tracked but protected. The same holds for the plan or any other In-flight path. **Restore none of the row**, including the original three. Preserve the workflow edits and take the protected-path exit to the human.

### Independent R — redraw

12. The supplied second FAIL requires refund records, changing Goal/ACs. Classify it as a **redraw before any restore**. Preserve the existing batch with its commit, hand dirty paths to the human without restoration, and stop for redraw authorization; the amendment grant does not supply it. On authorization, keep the worktree/spec, clear the plan tracker, reset/start brainstorm tracking, remove the plan and any loop ledger, and resume step 4 with the approved spec as draft. Required reference reads still apply.

### Equivalent plain-jj restore

13. For an eligible row only, use jj instead of git checkout:
   ```sh
   jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
   ```
   `root:` anchors the fileset to the workspace root; `-R` alone does not change cwd-relative path resolution. U/P remain wholly ineligible under jj too.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved between Before and After on this sample: both traces check the three paths for tracked membership and protection, narrate exactly three quoted `git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout --` commands before the `amended the spec:` apply, preserve the artifacts and In-flight paths, re-dispatch with an Amend-only block quoting the FAIL lines and baseline row, read the plan then reopen Task 1 in_progress then make one `amend:` batch commit, route U/P whole-row to step 6 with no partial restore, and in R commit as-is and hand paths to step 6 before any restore. The one shared failure is the commit fact: both audits write a placeholder for the retry item's evidence (Before `<FAIL lines + dirtied row, verbatim>`, After `<verbatim FAIL lines>; <dirtied row>`) even though the FAIL lines and dirtied row were supplied verbatim in the input and the fact keys on them appearing in the audit; After even quotes the FAIL lines verbatim in its hold table (step 5) and then still substitutes a placeholder in the commit body. To keep this fact while delivering the Change, the section-5 commit template should state that the audit's evidence column copies the held item's evidence text itself (the verbatim FAIL lines and dirtied row joined on one line), reserving angle-bracket placeholders only for fields the trace was not given (the first item's handle, choice and reviewer line).

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After improved on this sample rather than regressing it. Before lost dispatch because it narrated an extra `Amend-apply:` plan-writer chain and then an `Amend:` re-dispatch whose evidence was only the placeholder `<verbatim FAIL lines and dirty-source row>`, so the supplied FAIL lines and dirtied row were never actually quoted in the dispatch; it lost commit because step 8 declared that the controlling implement-only route 'expressly skips' the final plan read, breaking the read → tracker → single amend commit order the fact requires. After drops the implement-only detour, quotes the FAIL lines and dirtied row verbatim inside the `Amend:` block under `Rule:`/`Evidence:`, narrates the final `read` of the amended plan before reopening Task 1 and committing once, and keeps restore (three quoted `git -C` checkouts after three `ls-files` checks, artifact and In-flight paths untouched, `root:` jj fileset with the -R caveat), grant (changed-Tests attribution, held item, grant re-read, `amended the spec:` line with no human menu), protected (U/P whole-row ineligible, no partial restore) and redraw (R commits as-is, hands dirt to the human before any restore, no retry item or re-dispatch) intact. To make the new wording more robust against the accepted-variance placeholder drift on other models, state explicitly in section 5 that the retry audit and re-dispatch must reproduce the FAIL line and dirtied-row text verbatim, not a summary token, and that After's P variant should name commit/discard/move and 'writing-plans step 6' exactly as U does so the protected fact does not depend on the reader inferring 'protected-path exit' means the same menu.
